coverage_summary: Reviewed all 11 trajectories against the supplied paper text. Most opaque module boundaries are appropriately unresolved, but the registered substructure route omits a documented branch and leaves stated preparation operations under-decomposed.

findings.detail: The preparation step is represented as one opaque boundary even though the paper explicitly states an ordered spatial split followed by removal: “we cut the structure ... into two halves with a plane, remove one of the halves and regenerate the missing half.” These correspond to a documented partition followed by selection/removal, with an intermediate node for the two halves.

evidence.quote: In the top row, we cut the structure of human dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR; PDB code 1DRF) into two halves with a plane, remove one of the halves and regenerate the missing half.

findings.required_change: Decompose prepare_partial_structure into partitioning by the plane and selecting/removing one partition, preserving unknown mask and representation details.

findings.detail: The trajectory is labeled as registered partial-structure regeneration but its only preparation step is specifically plane-based DHFR processing. The paper separately documents VHH complementarity-determining-region removal and reconstruction conditioned on the remaining framework; this branch is absent, consistent with the atlas seed's 12 routes versus 11 supplied trajectories.

evidence.quote: In the second row of Fig. 3b, we cut out the complementarity-determining regions of a VHH antibody and rebuilt them conditioned on the remaining framework structure.

findings.required_change: Add a separate VHH registered-substructure branch or trajectory: select/cut out the CDR region, retain the framework structure, and pass that retained framework to the same unresolved regeneration conditioner.
